caption: The drawing depicts a cylindrical stoneware crock with a slightly flared rim and two small, rounded handles on opposite sides near the top. The primary color of the crock is a grayish stone color, while decorative elements are painted in a cobalt blue. The upper part of the crock features a band of stylized floral or vine motifs with swirling patterns and leaf-like details encircling the vessel. There are additional horizontal blue bands near the top rim and spaced below the decorative floral band, as well as near the bottom of the crock. On the main body below the floral band, there are three simple blue decorative marks consisting of a central abstract motif flanked by two pairs of leaf or feather-like shapes. The background of the drawing is plain and off-white, and the artist's signature, "BETTY JACOB," appears near the bottom right.
title: 4 Gal Crock
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
